description: This is not the Vashlovani Visitor Centre — that is in Dedoplistskaro at 5 Baratashvili St (41.4625, 46.1036), ~40 km outside the bbox. This point is the park's Central Bungalows, called the 'Visitors Village' in the Council of Europe file: five two-person bungalows with a ranger station and picnic area, set a little off the main track between the Central Entrance and the Mijniskure border-guard post. An independent field guide places 'bungalows, a ranger station, and picnic area' at 41.1600, 46.5671 — 40 m from this node. It is one of only two places inside the park with bookable shelters (the other is Mijniskure); the APA route description says visitors 'overnight in the central bungalows or tents'. Suggested name_en: 'Central Bungalows (Visitors Village)'.

This is not a visitor centre; it is the Mijniskure bungalow and ranger complex. An independent guide gives 41.1117, 46.6462 for 'the other [bungalows] at Mijniskure' — the same point. The Council of Europe appraisal records six three-person bungalows at Mijniskure, and notes the Mijniskure bungalows were 'adapted to protection', i.e. they double as a ranger post. Suggested name_en: 'Mijniskure Bungalows and Ranger Station'.

spelling variants resolved. Georgian დათვისხევი; the APA's own English is 'Datviskhevi (Bear Gorge)' (written as one word in the official brochure), with 'Datvis Khevi' and 'Bear Canyon' also in common use. An independent guide places the camping/picnic area at the entrance to Bear Canyon at 41.2376, 46.3655 — 80 m from this node. Substance: a dry side-canyon off Pantishara with a marked walking loop of about 2.5 km (roughly 1–2 hours). One section requires scrambling up through a narrow gap in the rocks because the wooden walkway above is partly destroyed. A dedicated picnic area, parking and toilets are provided at the junction of Datviskhevi and the Pantishara valley.

The Georgian is პანტიშარას კანიონი = 'Pantishara Canyon'; OSM's name:en 'Pantishira' is a typo and should not be propagated. Standard English is 'Pantishara' (variants Pantishari, Pantyashara). Substance: a narrow gorge whose fortress-like vertical cliffs rise on both sides; the park track descends through it and emerges at the camping and picnic area at the mouth of Datviskhevi. Its strata were formed as sea bottom — mollusc shells are easily visible in the bare layers — and the canyon walls are where the swallow colonies that give the 'City of Swallows' its name are found. The APA route 'Pantishara – Datviskhevi' runs 55 km from the Dedoplistskaro visitor centre; an off-road vehicle is required.

ვაშლოვანის სახელმწიფო ნაკრძალი is the Vashlovani State Nature Reserve (also published as Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve); OSM's name:en 'Vashlivani' is a misspelling and must not be propagated. History: founded 1935 at 5,025 ha on the initiative of the botanist Niko Ketskhoveli and the forest scientist Vasil Gulisashvili; enlarged in 1989 to 8,034 ha when Mijniskure and Usakhelo were attached; in 2003 the Vashlovani Protected Areas were created around it, comprising the reserve, the National Park (25,021 ha) and three natural monuments — Alazani Floodplain Forest / Kaklis Kure (204 ha), Eagle Gorge (100 ha) and Takhti-Tepa (9.7 ha). The Protected Areas hold the Council of Europe European Diploma (awarded 2015) and are an Emerald Network site. NOTE the node's coordinate sits at Mijniskure, not at the reserve centroid, so it should not be used to place a reserve label.

The principal in-park accommodation: 9 of the park's 16 two-person bungalow shelters, sited in the Natlistsklis (Lekistskali) gorge per Annex N4 of the management plan, with a designated picnic site. Route 7 (Bugha Moedani - Shavi Mta) overnights here. Bungalow tariff 40 GEL double; camping 5 GEL per person; tents hired at the visitor centre. Coordinate is OSM way 1322451821, tagged tourism=hostel, name "ვიზიტორთა ცენტრი Central Bungalows" / name:en "Vashlovani Visitor Center".

name_en: Mijniskure visitor facility and bungalow camp
description: The park's riverside base on the Alazani in the far south-east, reached by descending from the Usakhelo viewpoint: 6 of the 16 bungalows (triple bungalow 50 GEL), one of the four 20-person campsites, a picnic site and the park's designated fly-fishing water — the Alazani holds ~20 fish species including wels catfish, carp, pike-perch, Caspian shemaya and shad, best in spring and autumn. Terminus of routes 5, 6 and 8. Coordinate is OSM node 1182746361, tourism=hostel, "ვიზიტორთა ცენტრი (Visitor Center)"; the Mijniskure locality node is 41.11210/46.64827 and Pshaveliskure locality 41.11416/46.64545.

Floodplain site holding the single isolated bungalow of the park's 16 (Annex N4) plus one of the seven designated picnic sites, on the Mijniskure - Shavi Mta axis. The management plan notes that Takhistskali and Ghoristskali (ღორისწყალი) are the same watercourse and that its bed is dry for most of the year, flowing only after rain, often as debris flows. Coordinate is the OSM locality node 760262910 (ტახის წყალი). A search snippet suggested a new ranger station is being built here, but no fetchable source confirmed it, so no station is reported.

name_en: Datviskhevi (Bear Gorge) and its picnic site
description: Side gorge off Pantishara carrying the park's palaeontological walking trail, and one of the seven picnic sites designated in the management plan. Fossilised woody plants and seashells are exposed between rock layers, proving the area was once under water, and southern-elephant bones were excavated here. Coordinate is OSM node 11792582004, name "დათვისხევი" / name:en "Bear Canyon"; a second board "დათვის ხევი" sits at 41.23769/46.36554.

The park's signature canyon, 50-55 km from the visitor centre and the start of routes 2, 7 and 8. Vertical fortress-like cliffs on both sides; the road in runs along the boundary between two landscapes, with the delicate xerophytic Nagomrebi ridge on the right and the Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve 50-70 m below on the left. The management plan lists it among the arid-woodland and clay-badland landscape units and notes the gorge bed is dry most of the year. Coordinate is OSM node 11792574788 (tourism=attraction); a Pantishara Valley board sits at 41.22787/46.35112 and a Pantishara plain board at 41.19274/46.35700.

to the metre by an independent source, which gives 41.1390, 46.5798 for the in-park 'border guard post'. This is a Georgian border-police checkpoint inside the National Park, less than 4 km south of the Central Bungalows, on the only road down to Mijniskure. Visitors must show passport, vehicle documents, the free Border Zone Permit issued by the Border Police in Dedoplistskaro (41.4723, 46.0854) and the paperwork from the Vashlovani Visitor Centre in order to pass. It is a permit-CHECKING post, not where permits are obtained. Suggested name_en: 'Mijniskure border-guard post'.

5.56 ha of open water detected in Sentinel-2 imagery of 2025-08-30 (MNDWI consensus). Reverse-geocodes to Qakh District, Azerbaijan — beyond the Alazani, in the irrigated lowland, so almost certainly an irrigation or fish pond rather than a semi-desert pool. Cross-referencing showed 11 of the 15 detected bodies lie in Azerbaijan and that 90.5% of all detected water area sits within 60 m of the Alazani — this is one river, not a set of park pools. Extent is date-specific.

name_en: Alazani Floodplain Forest Natural Monument (Kaklis Kure / Walnut Bay)
description: 204.4 ha of liana-hung riparian forest at 165 m in a peninsula-shaped bight of the Alazani riverbed, the only stretch of the river where the floodplain forest survives intact and the only place in Georgia with extensive natural stands of common walnut, oak, ash and elm — hence the name Walnut Bay. The entry neck is only 30-40 m wide and the forest is so dense that 1 km of the pedestrian route takes an hour. 56-60 km from Dedoplistsqaro (~1.5 h); entrance fee 5 GEL; picnic area at the monument. Coordinate is the official value N41 21.548 E46 39.235 from nationalparks.ge, corroborated by the OSM locality node კაკლის ყურე at 41.36568/46.65535. NOTE: English Wikipedia's infobox coordinate 41.69917/46.06444 is wrong and contradicts its own text.

name_en: Ancient pistachio grove (oldest pistachio tree in Europe)
description: Grove of wild pistachio (Pistacia, Georgian საკმლის ხე) reached by a short trail from the Vashlovani ranger station: most trees are over 500 years old and the oldest is over 900, advertised as the oldest pistachio in Europe. The species is Red-Listed in Georgia and abundant here; the park's name is popularly explained by the resemblance of these open pistachio stands to apple orchards. Coordinate is the OSM natural=tree node 10836240203 ("Old Pistachio"), with a "Flora" interpretive board at the same point.

Named cliff face in the Pantishara gorge where swallows have colonised the vertical rock in such numbers that the park calls it a city; a headline attraction of route 2. Coordinate is the OSM interpretive node 4424086000, name "მერცხლების ქალაქი" / name:en "city of swallows".

Marked locality on the Datviskhevi trail where the fossil bones of a southern elephant (Archidiskodon meridionalis) were excavated, the largest a shoulder bone about 87 cm long; the excavated material is now held in the protected areas administration building in Dedoplistsqaro. The park also advertises million-year-old plant and animal fossils and mammoth remains on its territory. Coordinate is OSM node 11792396535 (tourism=attraction).

but SUBSTANCE NOT FOUND. რკინის სადნობი სახელოსნო translates exactly as 'iron-smelting workshop' (სადნობი = smelting, სახელოსნო = workshop); 'Iron-smelting workshop (ruins)' is a correct rendering. OSM tags it ruins=building, mapped in the same July 2021 changeset as Khoranta, 2.5 km west-north-west of it, sourced from the Georgian cultural-heritage register. I found no description, dating or excavation report for this site in any APA, Council of Europe, academic or tourism source I could reach — and notably the APA's own list of Vashlovani cultural remains (Khoranta, Upadara, Kaladara, Black Mountain Monastery, Samukhi fortress, Pantishara and Mijnis Bay watchtowers) does NOT mention iron smelting. Do not assert a period. SRTM 174 m.

against an official source. The Agency of Protected Areas writes 'City of Khoranta' in English, listing it with 'villages Upadara and Kaladara' among the remains of ancient cities and villages in Vashlovani. Georgian ხორანთის ნაქალაქარი = 'the ruined town of Khoranta' (ნაქალაქარი = site of a former town). Recommended name_en: 'Khoranta ruined town (City of Khoranta)'. OSM tags it ruins=village with historic:civilization=medieval, sourced explicitly from the Georgian National Agency for Cultural Heritage Preservation's immovable-monuments register (memkvidreoba.gov.ge), added in July 2021 in one batch with three other ruins. SRTM 214 m; a Georgian POI directory gives about 205 m. Access note: the Dedoplistskaro tourism association states the municipality's archaeological sites are not on any tourist route and are not prepared to receive visitors. as an OSM information=board, English name already correct. Usable substance: the park's canyons are cut into Neogene and Quaternary marine and continental sediments; geological analysis shows the area was repeatedly sea bottom, confirmed by marine fauna preserved in the rock strata, and shells of molluscs are easily noticeable in the bare layers of Pantishara Canyon and Datvi gorge.

მერცხლების ქალაქი = 'City of Swallows'; the APA brochure uses 'city of swallows' and nationalparks.ge 'Swallow City'. Substance: on both sides of the narrow Pantishara gorge, fortress-like vertical cliffs rise, and swallows have built their nests in them in such numbers that the place is named after them. It is one of the two headline attractions of the APA's Pantishara–Datviskhevi route. Recommended pin name: 'City of Swallows (Mertskhlebis Kalaki)'.

Same feature as bear-canyon-8, mapped twice in OSM (დათვის ხევი here, დათვისხევი there, 65 m apart). The preferred English is the APA's 'Datviskhevi (Bear Gorge)'; 'bear ravine' is a non-standard rendering. These two nodes and the trail-map node should be treated as one site for pin purposes.

ავტოგზის დასასრული = 'end of the vehicle road'. Better English: 'End of vehicle track'. It sits 300 m from the Datviskhevi trailhead cluster, so it almost certainly marks where driving stops and the Bear Gorge foot trail begins, but no source describes this specific sign.

as an OSM information=board at Mijniskure, English name already correct. Usable substance: the Alazani floodplain forest is a liana-covered riparian forest of walnut, ash, oak and elm. The protected example is the Alazani Floodplain Forest (Kaklis Kure) Natural Monument, 204 ha, a peninsula-shaped bight in the Alazani bed with an entry point only 30–40 m wide; it is the only bight along the Alazani where this vegetation survives and the only place in Georgia with natural extensive stands of common walnut and common oak. 'Kaklis Kure' literally means 'bight of the walnut trees'. CAUTION: the Natural Monument itself is at 41.3536, 46.6502, not at this board.

'საფეხმავლო ბილიკი ჯვრისკენ' = 'Footpath to the cross'. This is the signed trailhead of the short walking trail from the Shavi Mta picnic area up to the cross on the Black Mountain convent ruins; an independent guide calls it a '(very) short hiking trail to a monastery' starting shortly after the designated picnic area at 41.2644, 46.6346, which is 50 m from this node.

and equivalence established. ლეკის (მლაშე) წყალი reads 'Lekis (Mlashe) Tskali' — the stream is known by two names: Lekistskali ('Lek's water', after the Lezgin/Dagestani highlanders) and Mlashetskali ('salty water', მლაშე = brackish). The one-word form 'Lekistskali' is the spelling used in the Council of Europe European Diploma appraisal, which names 'the Lekistskali gorge' — with the Kumuro and Bugha-Moedani areas — as one of the places where desert, steppe and arid-woodland plant communities form the park's most complex mosaic. The Georgian Wikipedia entry for the park also lists the river Lekistskali. OSM's Russian name for this board is 'Соленая вода' (salt water). The board sits on the stream at about 200 m, 600 m north of the in-park border-guard post. Practical note for the pin: the park has no drinkable surface water — the only supply is the well at Mijniskure.

Same place as mijniskure-21: this is the OSM interpretive-information node at the Mijniskure site (tourism=information, no name:en in OSM). 'Mijniskure' is the correct and standard English rendering. It is the only place in Vashlovani with a reliable water source — a well — which is the main reason multi-day trekking in the park is impractical; there is no water at any other ranger station or campsite.

as an OSM information=map board (a trail map panel), not a trail itself. The name matches the APA's official route 2, 'Pantishara – Datviskhevi (Bear Gorge)': 120 km round trip from Dedoplistskaro, one day, medium difficulty, off-road vehicle or bicycle combined with 3–4 km of walking. Listed attractions: the City of Swallows, Pantishara Alesilebi, fossil flora and fauna, the Vashlovani basin and ancient pistachio trees.

The Georgian is პანტიშარას ხეობა = 'Pantishara Valley'; OSM's name:en 'Pantissara' is a typo. Substance: the valley is the park's main western approach, about 13 km beyond the last settlement, Kasristskali, and roughly where the track crosses into the Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve. On the descent the road runs along the edge of two landscapes — the Nagomrebi ridge with xerophytic vegetation to one side and, 50–70 m below on the other, the Strict Nature Reserve cut by steep slopes, arid forest and deep gorges.

substance not found. ფიქალების ხევი = 'gorge of the shales' (ფიქალი = shale/slate); the OSM node also carries name:de 'Schieferschlucht' (shale gorge), so 'Pikalebis Khevi (Shale Gorge)' is a correct rendering. No published description of this particular gorge exists in the APA, Council of Europe or tourism literature I searched. Generic context that is safe to use: the park's relief is built on Neogene and Quaternary sedimentary rock, and eroded ravines and badlands dominated by juniper and pistachio woodland are its characteristic landform.

as an OSM information=board (one of the park's interpretive panels), name already in English. Usable substance: Vashlovani's semi-desert is the reason the park is often compared to an African or Wild West landscape. The climate is dry subtropical, one of the hottest in Georgia, with summer temperatures reported up to 50–55 °C, months without rain, and snow so rare that several years may pass without it. The Eldari lowland here is the only place in Georgia where true semi-desert has developed.

The Georgian 'რეინჯერსთა საგუშაგო' is generic ('rangers' post'); this specific post is the Shavi Mta (Black Mountain) ranger station, given as 41.2711, 46.6285 by an independent guide — identical to this node. The Council of Europe appraisal lists 'Shavi mta' among the park's protection stations. It sits at ~796 m on a forested ridge reached by a muddy forest track past the picnic area; beyond it are views over the Alazani valley and, in clear weather, the Greater Caucasus. Distances given: 28 km from Mijniskure ranger station, 13 km down to the Kaklis Kure floodplain-forest station, 61 km back to the Dedoplistskaro visitor centre via Kvemo Kedi. Suggested name_en: 'Shavi Mta (Black Mountain) Ranger Station'.

name_en: Shavi Mta car park & picnic area
description: 'მანქანის გასაჩერებელი და საპიკნიკე' = 'car park and picnic area'; an independent guide gives 41.2644, 46.6346 for the 'designated picnic area' on Shavi Mta — the same point to within 20 m. It is the road-head for the Black Mountain monastery walk and one of the park's seven picnic areas listed in the Council of Europe appraisal.

as an OSM information=board at the Datviskhevi trailhead, and this is the anchor for the fossil elephant story. Substance: the strata here were laid down as sea bottom, and mollusc shells are easily visible in the bare layers — the oldest inhabitants of Vashlovani. In Datvis Khevi, bones of a southern elephant were found; the largest is 87 cm long and is dated to about 2 million years. Sources disagree on which bone: the APA brochure says only 'the largest, 87 cm in length', nationalparks.ge calls it a shoulder bone, the Council of Europe appraisal a back bone. The excavated bones are held in the Protected Areas administration building in Dedoplistskaro. NOTE for the pin: no source gives a coordinate for the find spot, and a field guide reports there are no boards or signs marking it on the ground — so the find site must not be given an invented coordinate; use this board node or the Dat

Transliteration 'Bughdalu' (ბუღდალუ) is straightforward, but no published source describes the place. Reverse geocoding confirms it is in Dedoplistsqaro Municipality, Kakheti, Georgia, on the Sabatlo–Black Mountain track, at about 213 m. The -lu ending is Turkic, as with neighbouring Sabatlo, which is characteristic of toponyms in this Eldari/Shiraki winter-pasture belt. Pin it as a locality with no further claim.

'Mijniskure' is the spelling used by the APA and nationalparks.ge; 'Mijnis Kure' and 'Mijnis Bay' also appear in APA English texts, and 'Midjniskure'/'Mijniskhure' in third-party sources. Georgian მიჯნის ყურე = 'boundary bight' (მიჯნა boundary, ყურე bay/bight); a Georgian magazine glosses it as 'edge' or 'outpost'. It is Georgia's south-easternmost outpost, the point where the Alazani crosses into Azerbaijan, and is the first place in the country to see sunrise. SRTM puts it at 95 m, in the Eldari Lowlands — eastern Georgia's lowest ground at about 90 m. Bungalows, camping, picnic benches, a water well and designated fly-fishing on the Alazani (about 20 fish species, including wels catfish, common carp, pike-perch, Caspian shemaya and shad; best in spring and autumn). Mijniskure and Usakhelo were added to the state reserve in 1989, enlarging it to 8,034 ha. Reachable only after passing t

Transliteration 'Pshaveliskure' is a reasonable rendering of ფშაველისყურე, but I found no published source for the place at all. The name element -ყურე (kure, 'bight/bend') is the same as in Mijniskure and Kaklis Kure, both of which are bights of the Alazani, and ფშაველი means a person from Pshavi, a Georgian highland province whose shepherds traditionally wintered in these lowlands — so 'Pshavian's bight' is a plausible reading, but it is an etymological inference, not a sourced fact. It lies 260 m from the Mijniskure bungalows at about 102 m elevation.

ტახის წყალი is written 'Takhistskali' by OSM and by the tourism literature, and 'Takhis tskali' on the APA trail names; literally 'wild boar's water' (ტახი = wild boar). An independent guide gives 41.1567, 46.6512 — identical to this node. It is a locality on the Alazani a few kilometres north of Mijniskure, reached by a riverside track past wind-sculpted cliffs rising over savanna; the finest scenery near Mijniskure per that guide. The Mijniskure–Takhistskali section is the National Park's strict-protection zone, where winter grazing and livestock shelters were prohibited under the European Diploma conditions. A new ranger station has been under construction here. SRTM 113 m.

'Qəbirstanlıq' is not a proper name — it is the ordinary Azerbaijani common noun for a cemetery or graveyard, and OSM tags it landuse=cemetery. It should be labelled 'Cemetery' (optionally 'Cemetery, Lələli'), not carried as a place name. It lies in Qakh District, Azerbaijan, beside Lələli village, outside Georgia and outside the park.

and worth a substantive note: the Georgia–Azerbaijan boundary here follows the Alazani and has never been formally delimited — a Georgian magazine account states the border 'has yet to be delimited and defined', which is why border-police registration and a Border Zone Permit are compulsory for the whole eastern half of Vashlovani and why an in-park checkpoint controls the road to Mijniskure. The Council of Europe appraisal records that Georgia and Azerbaijan jointly run the goitered gazelle reintroduction across this border.

პატარა შირაქი = 'Patara Shiraki', literally 'Little Shiraki'; Russian-language tour operators call the same ground 'the Little Shiraki prairies'. Shiraki is the wheat plain between the Iori plateau and the Alazani plain, nicknamed Georgia's granary; the approach road from Dedoplistskaro crosses it, and it is at its most striking in late spring when the wheat ripples. OSM maps this polygon as farmland, which is consistent. Keep the English as 'Patara Shiraki (Little Shiraki)'.

Established 2003, IUCN category II, administered by the Agency of Protected Areas. Area figures conflict across official sources: 24,610.06 ha in the Georgian government's 2012 protected-areas situation analysis, 250.2 km² reported area in WDPA/Protected Planet (site 555549413), 251.14 km² on Wikipedia. Coordinate is the centroid of OSM relation 6135120 (tagged boundary=national_park, wikidata Q2097137); Wikipedia's infobox instead gives 41.200/46.383 and Wikidata 41.2/46.38333, both of which fall in the western half of the polygon.

name_en: Vashlovani Strict Nature Reserve (State Nature Reserve)
description: Founded 1935 on the initiative of Niko Ketskhoveli and Vasil Guliashvili; IUCN category Ia, 10,143 ha of which 4,032 ha forest, the rest fields, semi-desert and ravines, at 300-600 m. The management plan states explicitly that the reserve contains NO zones, unlike the national park. Strictly off-limits to general visitors — the Pantishara route only overlooks it from the Nagomrebi side. Coordinate is the published Wikipedia/Wikidata point (41°09'17.5"N 46°32'49.6"E); OSM relation 6135198 centroid is 41.18336/46.47532.

AND CAUTION. OSM's 'usakhelo-mta' should be 'Usakhelo Mta', literally 'Nameless Mountain' (უსახელო = nameless). The APA and nationalparks.ge call the associated lookout the 'Usakhelo Viewing Point' / 'viewpoint of Usakhelo' — the famous stop on the descent from the Central Entrance to Mijniskure, with a triangular viewing platform built out over an outcrop and an information board, overlooking badlands to the east and south. IMPORTANT: the viewing platform is at 41.1272, 46.6070 per an independent guide, about 1.1 km north-east of this OSM peak node (OSM ele 428 m, SRTM 420 m). Do not use this node as the viewpoint pin. Usakhelo, with Mijniskure, was attached to the state reserve in 1989; shepherd-owned land near the Usakhelo viewpoint was later re-designated from reserve to National Park after 2016 demarcation.

name_en: Usakhelo Mta (Nameless Mountain) and Usakhelo viewpoint
description: Peak of 428 m whose massif is one of the three named viewpoints in the management plan and the panorama over the badlands that routes 5 and 6 cross before descending to Mijniskure. The whole Usakhelo massif, with the lower Natlistskali and the Mijniskure gorge, forms the national park's strict nature protection zone. Coordinate is the OSM peak node 8061747863 (უსახელო-მთა, ele=428).

'Zilcha' (ზილჩა) is OSM's own transliteration and appears in no source I could find outside OSM, so the spelling is unverified. OSM tags it 845 m; SRTM30m gives 837 m, against a park maximum of 858 m — i.e. this is effectively the highest ground in Vashlovani. It lies 17 m from the cross on the Black Mountain convent ruins, so it is the summit point of the Shavi Mta (Black Mountain) ridge, described in Georgian sources as 'the tallest mountain in the Shiraki Valley', dark-looking because of its forested slopes, with views to the Alazani valley and the Caucasus. The equation Zilcha = Shavi Mta summit is my inference from position and elevation, not a sourced statement.

Same named place as bugha-moedani-14, mapped a second time in OSM as natural=plateau 900 m to the north (OSM name:ru 'Бычья арена'). SRTM 241 m. Treat the two nodes as one site; 'Bugha Moedani' is the correct English form in both cases. It is both a named area of the park and one of its ranger protection stations.

One of the eight permanent 24-hour ranger protection stations listed in the 2013 management plan, and the operational hub deepest inside the park. Coordinate is OSM way 474150182, tagged building=office, name "rangerpost", standing ~40 m from the Central Bungalows compound — the two form one enclosure. Rangers here run scheduled weekly patrol routes assigned per sector; in 2013 the protection division comprised a head, 2 senior rangers and 23 rangers.

name_en: Kaklis Kure ranger protection station and campsite
description: One of the eight permanent ranger stations, one of the four that double as a park entrance, and the site of one of the four 20-person campsites plus a picnic site — it controls access to the Alazani Floodplain Forest Natural Monument. Position is the OSM locality node for კაკლის ყურე (760262890) used as a proxy; the official monument coordinate 41.35913/46.65392 lies ~800 m south-south-west. North of the NP bbox because this unit sits outside the main park polygon on the Alazani.

One of the eight permanent 24-hour ranger stations named in the 2013 management plan. No source gives its own coordinate; the position here is the OSM Mijniskure locality node (760262846) used as a proxy, since the station shares the Mijniskure riverside compound with the bungalows, campsite and picnic site. The whole Mijniskure gorge falls inside the national park's strict nature protection zone, so ranger presence here governs access.

name_en: Shavi Mta (Black Mountain) ranger station and campsite
description: One of the eight permanent ranger stations and one of the four stations that double as a park entrance; also one of the four 20-person campsites and one of the seven picnic sites. Coordinate is OSM node 4424146593, tourism=information, name "რეინჯერსთა საგუშაგო" / name:en "rangers post". The associated parking-and-picnic node is at 41.26449/46.63466 and the trailhead for the footpath to the monastery cross at 41.26487/46.63523; Zilcha peak (845 m) stands 200 m east.

One of the eight permanent 24-hour ranger stations and one of the four that double as a park entrance; also the site of one of the four 20-person campsites, one of the seven picnic sites and the park's one purpose-built viewpoint. The trekking map places it on the Pantishara route immediately before the trail to the ancient pistachio grove, and describes trekkers reaching it after descending from the Pantishara gorge. No source publishes its coordinate: the position given is the OSM "Old Pistachio" tree node (10836240203), which marks that adjacent grove, so treat it as indicative to ~1 km rather than surveyed.

name_en: Voliere (goitered gazelle enclosure) multifunctional protection station, Bugha Moedani
description: One of the eight permanent ranger stations, opened in December 2012 as a multifunctional protection station at the goitered gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa) breeding enclosure on the Bugha Moedani plain, inside the national park's restoration zone. It is the operational base of Georgia's first successful reintroduction programme, running since 2013 and now supporting up to ~150 animals; the plain and the Qumuro flats were the species' last natural refuge before its 20th-century extirpation. Position derived from the OSM Bugha Moedani plateau node (9677524553); the associated viewpoint node is 41.12431/46.53801.

name_en: Cross on the Black Mountain convent ruins
description: as the ruins of the Shavi Mta (Black Mountain) convent. The Georgian 'ჯვარი ნამონასტრალზე' correctly renders as 'Cross on the site of the former monastery'. The APA lists 'remains of Black Mountain Monastery' among Vashlovani's cultural monuments; the site is a 4th–5th century nunnery of which, per the APA brochure, 'only fragments of the floor and foundation can be seen'. By tradition Queen Ketevan the Martyr spent her last night in Georgia here before being taken through the Eldari Lowlands to Persia, where she was killed in 1624 for refusing to convert to Islam. A field guide describes a '(very) short hiking trail to a monastery' starting just past the picnic area at 41.2644, 46.6346 — 210 m from this node, which sits on the 835 m ridge crest.
name_en_prev: Cross on the former monastery site

name_en: Shavi Mta Monastery ruins (cross on the former monastery site)
description: Ruins of a 4th-5th century church on Black Mountain, of which only fragments of the floor and foundation survive; by legend Queen Ketevan the Martyr spent her last night here before leaving for Persia. Named in the official APA sightseeing list as "remains of Black Mountain Monastery" and the destination of routes 5 and 7. Reached by a marked footpath from the Shavi Mta ranger station (trailhead node 41.26487/46.63523). 180 ha of the national park's Shavi Mta territory was transferred to the Khornabuji and Hereti Eparchy for 20 years by Presidential decree №734 of 30 Dec 2007. Coordinate is the OSM place_of_worship node 4424146895, "ჯვარი ნამონასტრალზე" (cross on a former monastery site) — the identification with the convent is strong but inferred from position and context rather than stated.

Lələli is a village in Qakh District, Azerbaijan — not in Georgia and not in the park. Nominatim renders it 'Lalali'. Recommended English label: 'Lələli (Lalali), Qakh District, Azerbaijan'. It sits on the east bank of the Alazani opposite the northern tip of the study area.

Official route 2: visitor centre to Pantishara gorge (50-55 km), 130 km roundtrip, 1 day, medium; bicycle or off-road vehicle integrated with 3-4 km of hiking. Attractions are the city of swallows, the Pantishara Alesilebi badlands, plant and animal fossils, the Vashlovani basin and the ancient pistachio grove. On the Datviskhevi trail fossilised wood, seashells and the bones of a southern elephant were found, the largest 87 cm long and now kept in the administration building. Coordinate is the OSM trailhead information node "Pantishara - Datvis Khevi (Bear Gorge)" (10836250941); a "Fossilized World of Vashlovani" board sits at the same spot and the motor road ends at 41.23891/46.36249.

name_en: Route 4: Kaklis Kure - Alazani Floodplain trail
description: Official route 4: visitor centre to Kaklis Kure (60 km), 120 km roundtrip, 1 day, medium, off-road vehicle; also run as a birdwatching tour. Goes south-east from Dedoplistsqaro through the villages of Zemo Kedi, Arkhilos Kalo and Kvemo Kedi to the Alazani Floodplain Forest Natural Monument, where there is a picnic area. No published line geometry.

name_en: Route 5: Mijniskure - Shavi Mta (Black Mountain) trail
description: Official route 5: 225 km roundtrip over 2 days, difficult, off-road vehicle plus 3-4 km hiking, from the visitor centre via the central entrance (50 km). Day 1 crosses the park past the Usakhelo viewpoint and descends to Mijniskure to overnight in bungalows or tents with fly fishing. Day 2 returns to the central entrance, follows the Imedi gorge to the Shavi Mta forest (common pheasant habitat) and a picnic area, then hikes the ridge to the Shavi Mta convent ruins, with the Alazani valley and the Mingachevir reservoir on the right. Highlights listed officially as the convent ruins, Heretis Foni, sport fishing and the Usakhelo view. No published line geometry.

Official route 6: 160 km roundtrip over 2 days, difficult, bicycle or off-road vehicle, from the visitor centre via the central entrance (50 km) and the Usakhelo viewpoint down to Mijniskure. Overnight in bungalows or tents on the riverbank, with picnic areas and the park's designated fly-fishing water on the Alazani; the official highlights are "Alesilebi and fly fishing". No published line geometry.

name_en: Route 7: Bugha Moedani - Shavi Mta trail
description: Official route 7: 200 km roundtrip over 2 days, moderate, off-road vehicle plus 3-4 km hiking, from the visitor centre to Pantishara gorge (50 km). Day 1 explores the gorge and the razor-sharp badlands, then a viewpoint over the Vashlovani basin with its pistachio and juniper, overnighting in the central bungalows or tents. Day 2 goes via the central entrance and the Imedi gorge to the Shavi Mta forest, its picnic area and the convent ruins. Sold on the paradox of standing in semi-desert while looking at the snow-capped Caucasus. No published line geometry.

name_en: Route 8: Land of the Hidden Water trail
description: Official route 8: 190 km roundtrip, 2 days (the English trip page says 1), difficult, off-road vehicle plus 3-4 km hiking, from the visitor centre to Pantishara gorge (50 km); it covers almost the whole national park. Day 1 runs through Pantishara south-east to the Samukhi valley — goitered gazelles may be seen at a distance and leaving the route to approach them is prohibited — then descends to Mijniskure. Day 2 passes through Chighoelta Khevi to a ranger station and a Vashlovani-basin viewpoint before returning. The theme is subsurface water: visitors are warned of ground holes several metres deep and told not to deviate from the path. No published line geometry.

No source found. 'Iatagi Dzori' is OSM's own transliteration of იატაგი ძორი; the second element is the Armenian word for gorge (dzor) and the first resembles Turkic 'yatag' (bed, lair, winter camp), so the name is a non-Georgian compound typical of this winter-pasture zone — but this is speculation, not a sourced etymology. Reverse geocoding places it at Sabatlo, Dedoplistsqaro Municipality, Georgia. Do not publish an English gloss.

სასაზღვრო მდინარე ალაზანი = 'Border Alazani River', i.e. a viewpoint over the reach where the Alazani becomes the Georgia–Azerbaijan boundary. Usable substance: this is the furthest point at which the Alazani can be seen crossing Georgia's border; from the bank at Mijniskure, and better from the hill above, the Mingachevir Reservoir and the mountains of Azerbaijan are visible. Suggested name_en: 'Alazani border-river viewpoint'.

'Alesilebi' is the APA's own English spelling (ალესილები, 'the sharpened ones'); the APA glosses the feature as 'Pantishara Alesilebi (razor-sharp badlands cliffs)'. The Georgian node name ალესილების ხედი means 'view of the Alesilebi'. Substance: these are exposed ancient seabeds that erosion has cut into pillars and columns resembling man-made castles; the Council of Europe appraisal treats 'Areulebi–Alesilebi' as a single landscape covering roughly 195 km² of the park — a natural labyrinth of interconnected, often vertical dry gullies with precipices up to 70 m, holding arid juniper and pistachio open woodland, shibliak and desert vegetation. The cliffs are a favoured perch for eagles and griffon vultures. CAUTION: this is not the 'Pantishara Viewpoint', a separate and better-known lookout over the same cliffs at 41.2234, 46.4061, about 4.5 km east.

'Bugha Moedani' is the APA's and nationalparks.ge's own English spelling of ბუღა მოედანი, literally 'bull's square' or 'bull's arena' (Russian-language sources render it 'Бычья арена' / 'Buga Moedani (Bull's Arena)'). It names the park's official two-day route 'Bugha Moedani – Shavi Mta (Black Mountain)': about 200 km round trip from Dedoplistskaro, moderate, off-road vehicle with 3–4 km of hiking, with pistachio trees, juniper groves, the Vashlovani viewing point over the park's basin and the Shavi Mta broadleaf forest as its highlights. The Council of Europe appraisal names Bugha Moedani as one of the park's protection (ranger) stations and, with Kumuro and the Lekistskali gorge, as one of the areas with the most complex mosaic of desert, steppe and arid-woodland vegetation. SRTM 272 m.

Broad semi-desert plain in the south of the protected areas, giving its name to route 7 and hosting the goitered gazelle enclosure and its protection station. The management plan places it in the plains semi-desert landscape together with the middle and lower Lekistskali flats, and records that isolated gazelles survived on Bugha Moedani and the Qumuro flats until the end of the 20th century. Coordinate is OSM viewpoint node 4867606321; the plateau node 9677524553 is at 41.13247/46.53878.

LOCATION NOT. ექოს გადასახედი renders correctly as 'Echo Viewpoint' (გადასახედი = lookout/overlook). A named Echo viewpoint is a standard stop on Vashlovani safari itineraries, described as the top of a roughly 70-metre clay slope with views over the park's landscape, the outlines of the mountains and the Mingachevir Reservoir far on the horizon, and used as a picnic stop. That 70 m figure matches the Council of Europe description of precipices up to 70 m in the Areulebi–Alesilebi badlands. SRTM gives 466 m for this node, one of the higher points on the central park road. CAVEAT: the tour description places the Echo viewpoint between the Patara Shiraki plain and the descent into Pantishara valley, which does not obviously match this coordinate, and the OSM node is recent (September 2025) with no name:en. Treat the description as applying to the named feature, not verified for this exact

Viewpoint over the Alesilebi — razor-sharp eroded badland cliffs that look like man-made castles but are erosional pillars and columns; the park's most-photographed geology and listed as a highlight of routes 2, 6 and 7. Coordinate is OSM viewpoint node 11891968791 (ალესილების ხედი). A "Kasristskali-Pantishara-Alesilebi" road runs to it (way centre 41.24299/46.40687).

Qanıx (also Qanıxçay, and Alazan çayı) is the Azerbaijani name for the Alazani, so 'Alazani (Qanıx)' is a correct bilingual rendering; the preferred English label is simply 'Alazani'. The river rises in the Greater Caucasus in Kakheti, is the Kura's main tributary in eastern Georgia, forms part of the Georgia–Azerbaijan border, and ends in the Mingachevir Reservoir in Azerbaijan. Vashlovani's eastern edge is defined by it.

Same river as alazani-qan-x-45, tagged with only the Azerbaijani name. For an English-language map this should be labelled 'Alazani (Qanıx)' or 'Alazani' rather than 'Qanıx' alone, so that the two OSM ways read as one river.

The Council of Europe appraisal glosses the related landscape name Areulebi as 'a Georgian name that translates as a place where it is easy to get lost', and describes it as a network of mostly dry, often very deep and narrow gullies with eroded, sometimes vertical slopes, interconnected and curving, with very short visibility — 'a large natural labyrinth' — with precipices up to 70 m, covering roughly 195 km² of the park. არეული ხევი is best rendered 'Areuli Khevi (Tangled Gorge)'. Applying that gloss to this specific stream is an extension from the landscape name to the watercourse name, which the source does not make explicitly.

Transliteration confirmed as standard: ღორისწყალი = 'Ghoristskali', literally 'pig's water' (ღორი = pig). It is one of a pair of similarly named streams in the park with Takhistskali ('wild boar's water'), both referring to the wild boar that are among the park's characteristic mammals. No published description of the stream itself was found.

Same watercourse as lekis-mlashe-tskali-salt-water-12: მლაშეწყალი 'Mlashetskali', literally 'salt water', also called Lekistskali in the Council of Europe report and the Georgian Wikipedia park article. It drains the central park past the border-guard post towards the Alazani. A 24 km 'Mlashetskali – Bugha Moedani' water pipeline is reported in a second Council of Europe file on Vashlovani, but that document returned HTTP 403 and I could not read it directly, so treat the pipeline as unverified.

Weak lead only. The Council of Europe appraisal names a 'Kumuro' area, with Bugha-Moedani and the Lekistskali gorge, as one of the park's most complex desert/steppe/arid-woodland vegetation mosaics. Whether Kumuro is the same name as this stream, კუმრა 'Kumra', I could not establish — the spellings differ and no map in the sources ties them together. Do not publish the equivalence.

This is Əyriçay, an Azerbaijani river name meaning 'crooked river'; common English transliterations are Ayrichay or Eyrichay. Reverse geocoding places this point in Qakh District, Azerbaijan — outside Georgia and outside Vashlovani National Park. It should be labelled as an Azerbaijani feature, not a park feature.
